decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: proposed a release with “manual saving”; Round 1 client: “saving links ... matches what I pictured.”
decisions.note: The presented ability to save links conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “editing”; Round 1 client lists “editing” among the parts that match.
decisions.note: Bookmark editing was presented conformingly at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “deletion”; Round 1 client says “deleting” matches what she pictured.
decisions.note: Deletion was a conforming initial-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tags”; Round 1 client says tags match what she pictured.
decisions.note: Tag assignment was presented conformingly; the transcript does not establish a separate autocomplete decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “filtering”; Round 1 client identifies filtering among the matching capabilities.
decisions.note: The recorded filtering decision conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “search”; Round 1 client says search matches and explicitly states “Case-insensitive search is good.”
decisions.note: Basic full-text and case-insensitive search were conforming initial decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “sorting”; Round 1 client lists sorting among the matching capabilities.
decisions.note: Sorting conformed at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “manual saving.” Round 1 client reports that the draft requires typing a title and leaves automatic page details out, rejects that, and specifies fetching title, icon, description/preview while permitting edits before and after saving.
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the client replaces manual metadata entry with the reference-aligned automatic-fetch-and-edit behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “duplicate warnings.” Round 1 client identifies the offered behavior as warning while allowing both copies and says a repeated link should instead open the existing bookmark for updating.
decisions.note: The initial duplicate policy diverged; the client supplied the reference-conforming convergence-to-edit behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed scope does not include a read-later workflow. Round 1 client requests marking bookmarks unread, viewing only unread bookmarks, and marking them read when finished.
decisions.note: The client extends the initial specification with the missing unread/read-later flow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents deletion but no archive flow. Round 1 client says “Archiving, separate from deleting,” asks to hide without losing content, and requests an archived list.
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted reversible archive behavior and distinguishes it from permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes notes; Round 1 client identifies them as plain text and asks for headings, lists, links, and formatted rendering.
decisions.note: The client corrects the initial plain-note design to markdown-capable notes.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents basic search/filtering. Round 1 client requests tag shorthand, AND/OR/exclusion combinations, and exact phrases in quotes.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client surfaces and requests the missing advanced-search family.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s scope lacks bulk actions. Round 1 client asks to select several bookmarks for tag/read/archive/delete actions, “including everything currently matching my search or filter.”
decisions.note: The response adds both selected-item and current-filter collection bulk operations.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker does not present saved filters. Round 1 client asks to save and reuse a search with included and excluded tags.
decisions.note: The client extends the initial specification with bundles/saved searches.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly says “import/export are excluded for now.” Round 1 client calls that “a real gap” and requests import from and export to the standard bookmarks file.
decisions.note: The client rejects the explicit import/export exclusion at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker does not present personal display settings. Round 1 client requests default sort order, displayed-item count, and text size.
decisions.note: The response adds the missing display-preference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says all requested capabilities are included; Round 2 client specifically recognizes “Automatic details on save with the ability to edit.”
decisions.note: The revised specification presents the corrected metadata behavior conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies that URL fragments and superficial variations do not create duplicates; Round 2 client recognizes repeated links as taking her to the existing item.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-handling decision conforms; normalization is an equivalent strengthening.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker states all requested capabilities are included and makes new/imported bookmarks unread by default; Round 2 client recognizes the “read-later” flow.
decisions.note: The revised specification records a conforming unread workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says all requested capabilities are included; Round 2 client expressly recognizes “archive flows” and approves the revision.
decisions.note: The revised specification’s archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Notes support headings, lists, and links.” Round 2 client recognizes “formatted notes.”
decisions.note: The revised note decision conforms to markdown note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says all requested capabilities are included; Round 2 client recognizes search with tags, exact phrases, and combined conditions.
decisions.note: The revised advanced-search decision is recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says all requested capabilities are included; Round 2 client recognizes “acting on many at once.”
decisions.note: The revised bulk-management decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says all requested capabilities are included; Round 2 client recognizes “saving searches I reuse.”
decisions.note: The revised specification includes conforming saved filters/bundles.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies browser-compatible HTML export and import-related defaults; Round 2 client recognizes “bringing my bookmarks in and out.”
decisions.note: The revised import/export decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents newest-first, 25-per-page, and standard-text defaults; Round 2 client recognizes and approves the display preferences and defaults.
decisions.note: The revised display-settings decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker’s US1 covers safely retrieving page details, manual editing, saving, and reopening; Round 4 client approves the link-saved-and-editable milestone.
decisions.note: The implementation-task decision for automatic saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US2 Deduplication”; Round 4 client recognizes “preventing duplicates” and approves the tasks.
decisions.note: The deduplication task decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US3 Read/archive workflow”; Round 4 client recognizes that workflow and approves it.
decisions.note: The task-stage read and archive workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US4 Search and saved searches”; Round 4 client recognizes “search and saved searches.”
decisions.note: The task-stage search and bundle decision conforms to the previously corrected specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US5 Rich notes”; Round 4 client recognizes “rich notes.”
decisions.note: The implementation tasks preserve markdown-note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US6 Bulk management”; Round 4 client recognizes “bulk actions.”
decisions.note: The bulk-management task decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US7 Import/export”; Round 4 client recognizes “import/export.”
decisions.note: The task-stage import/export decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “US8 Display preferences”; Round 4 client recognizes those preferences.
decisions.note: The display-preference task decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents implemented “automatic page details”; Round 5 client reports that saving pulls in details and preserves edits, with a fallback icon.
decisions.note: The working-app presentation records conforming automatic-save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents implemented deduplication; Round 5 client verifies that capitalization or a trailing fragment still returns the existing bookmark rather than creating another.
decisions.note: The implementation-review duplicate decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents read/archive states; Round 5 client reports “Read-later, archive, and restore are all present.”
decisions.note: The working-app read/archive decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents formatted notes; Round 5 client confirms “rich formatted notes” are in place.
decisions.note: The implementation-review note decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “advanced and saved searches”; Round 5 client verifies tag shorthand, exact phrases, query interpretation, and saved searches.
decisions.note: The specifically evidenced implementation-review search decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents implemented bulk actions; Round 5 client confirms bulk selection is in place.
decisions.note: The implementation-review bulk-action decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents browser HTML import/export; Round 5 client verifies exporting a normal browser bookmarks file with tags and importing it back.
decisions.note: The working-app import/export decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents persistent display preferences; Round 5 client confirms those preferences are in place.
decisions.note: The implementation-review display-preference decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents the working app and its implemented scope without page snapshots. After testing, the Round 5 client explicitly identifies “keeping a saved copy of a page in case it disappears” as an idea “for down the road” and “a later round,” not a current acceptance blocker.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client independently surfaces the missing local-page snapshot expectation but explicitly accepts its deferral, so this is an accepted divergence rather than bare approval.
